rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulafan are night hours; zulfa can mean an hour, station, or nearness. Muzdalifa was said to derive from being a station after Arafat or from Adam approaching Eve there.
rows.anchor: وإن ذلك في سياق أمر الله بإقامة الصلوات، والوعد على إقامتها الجزيل من الثواب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Uthman reports the Prophet taught that the five daily prayers, with ablution and prayer, expiate sins between prayer times.
rows.anchor: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ وضوئي هذا، ثم قال: «من توضأ وضوئي هذا، ثم قام فصلى صلاة الظهر غفر له

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the good deeds that erase sins as saying tasbih, praise, the testimony of faith, and takbir.
rows.anchor: عن منصور، عن مجاهد، " {إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} [هود: 114] قال: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the five prayers, citing sound, recurrent prophetic reports and the verse's immediate context of the command to establish prayer.
rows.anchor: وأولى التأويلين بالصواب في ذلك قول من قال في ذلك: هن الصلوات الخمس، لصحة الأخبار عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a reminder for people who recall God's promise and hope for reward, and fear His warning; sealed hearts neither answer nor heed admonition.
rows.anchor: أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports a man confessed to an improper encounter short of intercourse; the Prophet recited the verse and said its lesson applied to everyone, not only the man.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: " جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال إني عالجت امرأة في بعض أقطار المدينة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In another report, a man described touching and kissing a woman without intercourse; after the verse was recited, the Prophet answered that its guidance was general.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله، أخذت امرأة في البستان

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports that the man was identified as an Ansari named Flan ibn Muattib and that the verse was revealed after his confession of an encounter short of intercourse.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، قال: " جاء فلان بن معتب رجل من الأنصار، فقال: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says a man committed an act short of adultery; the verse was revealed, and the Prophet said it benefits anyone among his community who acts on it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود: " أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة شيئا لا أدري ما بلغ

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman reports that the Prophet compared sins falling away through excellent ablution to dry leaves falling from a branch, then recited the verse.
rows.anchor: قال: كنت مع سلمان، فأخذ غصن شجرة يابسة فحته وقال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muadh reports that after a man confessed to an encounter short of intercourse, the Prophet instructed him to perform ablution and pray, and said the instruction was general to believers.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ، قال: " أتى رجل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله ما ترى في رجل لقي امرأة لا يعرفها

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports that a man seeking punishment was told that completing ablution and prayer with the Prophet cleansed his sin as at birth; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: سمع أبا أمامة، يقول: إن رجلا أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh reports the Prophet told a man who confessed to forbidden contact to make a thorough ablution and pray, then said the verse applied generally to Muslims.
rows.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل: أنه كان جالسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فجاء رجل

rows.speaker: أبو اليسر
rows.claim: Abu al-Yusr reports kissing a woman who came to buy dates; after consulting Abu Bakr and confessing to the Prophet, Gabriel brought the verse, which the Prophet said was for everyone.
rows.anchor: عن أبي اليسر بن عمرو الأنصاري، قال: أتتني امرأة تبتاع مني بدرهم تمرا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that a man who kissed a woman came to the Prophet saying he was ruined, and the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، " أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة، فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا نبي الله هلكت

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Sulayman al-Taymi reports a man struck a woman's buttock, sought counsel from Abu Bakr and Umar, and received no answer from the Prophet until this verse came down.
rows.anchor: عن معمر، عن سليمان التيمي، قال: ضرب رجل على كفل امرأة، ثم أتى أبا بكر وعمر

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata identifies the commanded prayers as the obligatory prayers in a report about a flour seller who kissed a woman and then sought guidance from Umar, Abu Bakr, and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء " في قول الله تعالى: {أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل} [هود: 114] أن امرأة دخلت

rows.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman reports a man of Banu Ghanm kissed a woman and placed his hand on her backside; after the verse was revealed, the man kept remembering its warning.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج، عن يزيد بن رومان، " إن رجلا من بني غنم، دخلت عليه امرأة فقبلها ووضع يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Muhammad to endure the harm and hardships inflicted by his people for God's sake, hoping for His great reward; God preserves the reward of every obedient person.
rows.anchor: يوفره أحوج ما يكون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report implies the Aziz's wife renewed her seduction and threatened imprisonment; Yusuf chose confinement over the sin she and the women invited him to commit.
rows.anchor: رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sijn means confinement or the prison house. Arabs use place nouns derived from verbs in place of verbal nouns; with fatḥa, sajN is a regular verbal noun.
rows.anchor: رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a reading with fatḥa on the first consonant was attributed to some early readers, al-Tabari rejects it because the authoritative readers agree against it.
rows.anchor: رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses what they invited Yusuf to as illicit sex.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه} [يوسف: 33] : من الزنا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Yusuf sought his Lord's aid and preferred prison to doing what God disliked.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " قال يوسف، وأضاف إلى ربه واستعانه على ما نزل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God does not repel their plotting, Yusuf says he may incline toward them and follow what they desire; ṣabā ilā means to lean or turn toward something.
rows.anchor: يقول: أميل إليهن، وأتابعهن على ما يردن مني، ويهوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line uses ṣabā for the heart inclining toward Hind; the verb may also be used transitively in the following hemistich.
rows.anchor: إلى هند صبا قلبي … وهند مثلها يصبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains aṣbu ilayhinna as following the women.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، " {أصب إليهن} [يوسف: 33] يقول: أتابعهن

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq glosses their plotting as what Yusuf feared from them and his inclination as a response to that danger.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن} [يوسف: 33] : أي ما أتخوف منهن {أصب إليهن}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says that without God's aid and protection, Yusuf could not prevent himself from yielding.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وإلا تصرف عني كيدهن أصب إليهن وأكن من الجاهلين} [يوسف: 33] قال: إلا يكن منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the ignorant means that by inclining to the women Yusuf would join those who disregard God's rights and disobey His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {وأكن من الجاهلين} [يوسف: 33] : أي جاهلا إذا ركبت معصيتك

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq glosses the phrase as being ignorant through committing God's disobedience.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {وأكن من الجاهلين} [يوسف: 33] : أي جاهلا إذا ركبت معصيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Yusuf did not state a separate request, his complaint that prison was preferable and conditional plea that God repel their plot implicitly asked God to protect him, so God answered that supplication.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم} [يوسف: 34] : أي نجاه من أن يركب المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording works pragmatically like a request: as a person may say, 'If you do not visit me, I will harm you,' implying that the listener should visit.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم} [يوسف: 34] : أي نجاه من أن يركب المعصية

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God saved Yusuf from committing sin with the women, although some of what he feared from them had already befallen him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {فاستجاب له ربه فصرف عنه كيدهن إنه هو السميع العليم} [يوسف: 34] : أي نجاه من أن يركب المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular verb in 'it appeared to them' refers to the Aziz, who is not named or individually specified; al-Tabari compares the construction with a report where one person speaks as 'the people.'
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، " {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات} [يوسف: 35] قال: كان من الآيات قد في القميص وخمش في الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing signs of Yusuf's innocence, they reversed their apparent decision to release him and decided to imprison him; the signs included the rear shirt tear, scratches on the face, and women's cut hands.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، " {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات} [يوسف: 35] قال: كان من الآيات قد في القميص وخمش في الوجه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the signs as the tear in Yusuf's shirt and scratches on the woman's face.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، " {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات} [يوسف: 35] قال: كان من الآيات قد في القميص

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the sign as the tear in Yusuf's shirt from behind.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات} [يوسف: 35] قال: قد القميص من دبر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the signs were the women's hand wounds and the tear in Yusuf's shirt.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، " {من بعد ما رأوا الآيات} [يوسف: 35] قال: الآيات: حزهن أيديهن، وقد القميص

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi lists the shirt and the women's cut hands among the signs.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {من بعد ما رأوا الآيات} [يوسف: 35] قال: الآيات: القميص، وقطع الأيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They intended to keep Yusuf imprisoned until they chose their next course; al-Tabari says God made this confinement a punishment for Yusuf's prior inclination toward the woman and an expiation.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، " {ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35] عثر يوسف عليه السلام ثلاث عثرات: حين هم بها فسجن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas relates three lapses: Yusuf's inclination led to prison, asking the cupbearer for help prolonged it, and his brothers' accusation of theft led to a brother's accusation against him.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، " {ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35] عثر يوسف عليه السلام ثلاث عثرات: حين هم بها فسجن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the Aziz's wife asked her husband either to let her leave and explain herself or imprison Yusuf because he was telling people she had solicited him.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35] قال: قالت المرأة لزوجها: إن هذا العبد العبراني قد فضحني في الناس

rows.speaker: أهل العربية من البصرة
rows.claim: One Basran grammatical explanation says the emphatic lām and nūn in la-yasjununnahu occur where an interrogative construction with ay would otherwise appear.
rows.anchor: {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35]

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: Some grammarians reject the interrogative explanation: the lām is an oath, since an emphatic nūn does not follow a question such as 'will you stand?'.
rows.anchor: {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35]

rows.speaker: نحوي من الكوفة
rows.claim: A Kufan grammarian says bada lahum carries the sense of 'they said/decided,' and speech can introduce either an oath or an interrogative, licensing the construction.
rows.anchor: {ثم بدا لهم من بعد ما رأوا الآيات ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35]

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima interprets the time until which Yusuf was imprisoned as seven years.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، " {ليسجننه حتى حين} [يوسف: 35] قال: سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits that Yusuf was first imprisoned; the youths' entry with him makes that missing event clear. They were servants of Egypt's senior king, one over drink and one over food.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " فطرح في السجن، يعني يوسف، ودخل معه السجن فتيان، غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the king as al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid and the two servants as Mujlith and Nabu, with Nabu responsible for drink.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " فطرح في السجن، يعني يوسف، ودخل معه السجن فتيان، غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر: الريان بن الوليد، كان أحدهما على شرابه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies one youth as the king's baker and the other as his cupbearer.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، " {ودخل معه السجن فتيان} [يوسف: 36] قال: كان أحدهما خبازا للملك على طعامه، وكان الآخر ساقيه على شرابه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the king jailed his baker for allegedly trying to poison him and jailed the cupbearer for suspected complicity.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " إن الملك غضب على خبازه، بلغه أنه يريد أن يسمه، فحبسه وحبس صاحب شرابه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Yusuf had announced he interpreted dreams, so the two youths pretended to have dreams to test his skill.
rows.anchor: عن أسباط، عن السدي، قال: " لما دخل يوسف السجن قال: أنا أعبر الأحلام

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the two companions of Yusuf had seen nothing and only feigned dreams to test his knowledge.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: «ما رأى صاحبا يوسف شيئا، وإنما كانا تحالما ليجربا علمه»

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq instead says they truly had dreams and admired Yusuf; Mujahid's account says Yusuf warned them that those who loved him had suffered trials, but they persisted in their affection.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " لما رأى الفتيان يوسف، قالا: والله يا فتى لقد أحببناك حين رأيناك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports Yusuf asked them not to love him, recalling that his aunt, father, and the Aziz's wife had loved him and that each love brought him hardship.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد " أن يوسف، قال لهم حين قالا له ذلك: أنشدكما الله أن لا تحباني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣiru khamran means 'I see myself pressing grapes'; Ibn Masud's reading makes the intended object, grapes, explicit.
rows.anchor: وعنى بقوله: {أعصر خمرا} [يوسف: 36] أي إني أرى في نومي أني أعصر عنبا

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya reports Ibn Masud's reading as 'I see myself pressing grapes'; the passage says Omanis call grapes khamr.
rows.anchor: عن محمد ابن الحنفية، قال " في قراءة ابن مسعود: «إني أراني أعصر عنبا»

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak also explains khamr here as grapes, saying this is the usage of Oman and some other region.
rows.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} [يوسف: 36] يقول: أعصر عنبا، وهو بلغة أهل عمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses khamr in this dream as grapes.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} [يوسف: 36] قال: عنبا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima gives the dreamer's fuller vision: he planted a vine, pressed its grapes, served the king, and was told he would leave prison after three days to serve him wine.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " أتاه فقال: رأيت فيما يرى النائم أني غرست حبلة من عنب، فنبتت، فخرج فيه عناقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'wil is what a matter ultimately leads or returns to; the youths ask Yusuf to tell them the outcome of what they saw in sleep.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {نبئنا بتأويله} [يوسف: 36] قال: به

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as asking Yusuf to tell them about the dream itself; Abu Ubayd explains interpretation as the thing to which a matter leads.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {نبئنا بتأويله} [يوسف: 36] قال: به

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains Yusuf's good conduct as tending the sick, helping the needy, and making room for those crowded in prison.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، قال: كنت جالسا معه ببلخ، فسئل عن قوله: " {نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين} [يوسف: 36] قال: قيل له: ما كان إحسان يوسف؟ قال: كان إذا مرض إنسان قام عليه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yusuf treated the sick, comforted the grieving, and strove in God's service; his encouragement gave despairing inmates patience and hope of reward.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، عن قتادة، قوله: " {إنا نراك من المحسنين} [يوسف: 36] قال: بلغنا أن إحسانه أنه كان يداوي مريضهم، ويعزي حزينهم

rows.speaker: يوسف
rows.claim: In Qatada's account, Yusuf identified himself as son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, while the prison keeper said he would give him the best confinement he could.
rows.anchor: فمن أنت يا فتى؟ قال: أنا يوسف ابن صفي الله يعقوب ابن ذبيح الله إسحاق بن إبراهيم خليل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the reports that Yusuf served inmates in practical ways. He answers that the youths call dream interpretation a kindness to them, like his other good deeds.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندنا بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن الضحاك وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although asking for a dream interpretation seems to praise knowledge, the phrase can mean: interpret it for us as a favor, just as you show goodness in your other actions.
rows.anchor: نبئنا بتأويل رؤيانا محسنا إلينا في إخبارك إيانا بذلك، كما نراك تحسن في سائر أفعالك

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes their praise of Yusuf as conditional: he would be one of the good-doers if he interpreted their dreams.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " استفتياه في رؤياهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who serves his master wine is the dreamer who saw himself pressing wine; the other, whose bread birds eat, will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.
rows.anchor: فيسقي ربه: يعني سيده وهو ملكهم، خمرا: يقول: يكون صاحب شرابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb here means master or king; qadiya al-amr means the matter being asked about is finished and God's decree upon them has taken effect.
rows.anchor: يقول: فرغ من الأمر الذي فيه استفتيتما، ووجب حكم الله عليكما بالذي أخبرتكما به

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the two youths denied having seen dreams after Yusuf interpreted them, but Yusuf said the matter was already decided.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " قال اللذان دخلا السجن على يوسف: ما رأينا شيئا فقال: {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان} [يوسف: 41]

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies Mujlith as the one crucified and Nabu as the one restored to his former service and accepted by his master.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " قال لمجلث: أما أنت فتصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسك، وقال لنبو: أما أنت فترد على عملك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the prediction had taken effect exactly as Yusuf interpreted when the youths claimed they had only been playing.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان} [يوسف: 41] عند قولهما: ما رأينا رؤيا إنما كنا نلعب

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj quotes the phrase 'in which you seek a decision' without adding a further gloss.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " {فيه تستفتيان} [يوسف: 41]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf knew the surviving cupbearer would be saved and asked him to tell his master of Yusuf's unjust imprisonment without a crime; rabb means the king or master.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " قال، يعني لنبو: {اذكرني عند ربك} [يوسف: 42] : أي اذكر للملك الأعظم مظلمتي، وحبسي في غير شيء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands the word ظن as uncertainty, since dream interpretation involves conjecture; al-Tabari rejects this application to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك} [يوسف: 42] وإنما عبارة الرؤيا بالظن، فيحق الله ما يشاء ويبطل ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari rejects reading Yusuf's prediction as conjecture: prophets cannot give a definite report that might prove false without undermining the proof of their message; Yusuf's firm prediction shows he knew it would occur.
rows.anchor: فأما الأنبياء فغير جائز منها أن تخبر بخبر عن أمر أنه كائن ثم لا يكون

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi reports that a companion at the prison door asked what to convey, and Yusuf asked to be remembered before his master, the king.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي، " أنه لما انتهى به إلى باب السجن قال له صاحب له. حاجتك أوصني بحاجتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reads Satan's causing forgetfulness as a lapse in Yusuf, who forgot to appeal to God; this lengthened his confinement and was painful punishment.
rows.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار، قال: " لما قال يوسف للساقي: {اذكرني عند ربك} [يوسف: 42] قال: قيل: يا يوسف اتخذت من دوني وكيلا

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar reports a divine reproach to Yusuf for taking an intermediary besides God, followed by Yusuf's lament that affliction had distracted his heart.
rows.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار، قال: " لما قال يوسف للساقي: {اذكرني عند ربك} [يوسف: 42] قال: قيل: يا يوسف اتخذت من دوني وكيلا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Several reports attributed to the Prophet say Yusuf's request that the cupbearer remember him caused him to remain in prison longer; Hasan wept and applied the lesson to people who turn to others in hardship.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لولا أنه» يعني يوسف «قال الكلمة التي قال ما لبث في السجن طول ما لبث»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a Prophetic report that Yusuf would not have remained so long had he not sought relief from someone besides God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لو لم يقل يوسف» يعني الكلمة التي قال «ما لبث في السجن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports a Prophetic saying that Yusuf's seeking intercession through the cupbearer prolonged his imprisonment as a punishment.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: «لولا أن يوسف استشفع على ربه ما لبث في السجن طول ما لبث

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Yusuf was not mentioned to the king until the king's dream; Satan made Yusuf forget his Lord and seek relief from the king, so he remained imprisoned as punishment.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قال: " قال له: {اذكرني عند ربك} [يوسف: 42] قال: فلم يذكره حتى رأى الملك الرؤيا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq instead says Satan made the cupbearer forget to tell the king about Yusuf; Yusuf's imprisonment then continued as punishment for asking the cupbearer to remember him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " لما خرج، يعني الذي ظن أنه ناج منهما، رد على ما كان عليه، ورضي عنه صاحبه. فأنساه الشيطان ذكر ذلك للملك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and Wahb report a seven-year prison term; Wahb lists it alongside Job's seven-year affliction and Nebuchadnezzar's seven years among beasts.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: «لبث يوسف في السجن سبع سنين»

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the duration of bid' here was seven years, matching Yusuf's prison term.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: " زعموا أنها، يعني البضع: سبع سنين، كما لبث يوسف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines bid' as three to nine years.
rows.anchor: سمعت قتادة، يقول: " البضع: ما بين الثلاث إلى التسع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid likewise defines bid' as three to nine years.
rows.anchor: عن إسرائيل، عن منصور، عن مجاهد، " {بضع سنين} [يوسف: 42] قال: ما بين الثلاث إلى التسع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines bid' as fewer than ten years.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج، قال ابن عباس: " {بضع سنين} [يوسف: 42] دون العشرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says bid' is used with tens, from ten through ninety, as an odd number within that range, but not with a hundred or thousand.
rows.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن البضع لا يذكر إلا مع العشر، ومع العشرين إلى التسعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari holds bid' ranges from three to nine and is never below three, following observed Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: والصواب في البضع من الثلاث إلى التسع إلى العشر، ولا يكون دون الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse does not explicitly say the king was asleep, Arabs understand 'I see myself doing this' as reporting a dream; seven fat cows, seven lean cows, and ears of grain are therefore a dream vision.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " إن الله أرى الملك في منامه رؤيا هالته، فرأى سبع بقرات سمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari glosses the seven green ears as dreamt ears, others as seven other ears, the mala' as nobles and associates, and aftuni as 'interpret it for me.'
rows.anchor: وسبع سنبلات خضر وأخر يابسات

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says God showed the king a frightening dream, after which he gathered diviners and interpreters; they called it confused dreams and admitted they could not interpret it.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " إن الله أرى الملك في منامه رؤيا هالته، فرأى سبع بقرات سمان

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the king as al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid and says he recognized the vision as true but did not know its interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " ثم إن الملك الريان بن الوليد رأى رؤياه التي رأى، فهالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surviving cupbearer says he will report the dream's interpretation and asks to be released to go to the person who knows it. The narrative omits that they released him and he went to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: قال: {أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون} [يوسف: 45]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah here means a long period or epoch; Ibn Ishaq's account identifies the survivor as Nabu, who remembered Yusuf after a long interval and brought him the king's dream.
rows.anchor: {وادكر بعد أمة} [يوسف: 45] : أي حقبة من الدهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the city, explaining the cupbearer's request to be sent to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {وقال الذي نجا منهما وادكر بعد أمة أنا أنبئكم بتأويله فأرسلون} [يوسف: 45] قال ابن عباس: لم يكن السجن في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Da'ban means habit or regular practice; Imru al-Qays uses it of someone's customary conduct toward Umm al-Huwayrith and her neighbor.
rows.anchor: قول امرئ القيس: [البحر الطويل] كدأبك من أم الحويرث قبلها … وجارتها أم الرباب بمأسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf advises seven years of customary cultivation and preserving the harvest in its ears, except a small amount for food; this is practical counsel to retain provisions.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " قال لهم نبي الله يوسف {تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا} [يوسف: 47]

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Yusuf's advice to sow for seven years was meant to build up reserves.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " قال لهم نبي الله يوسف {تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا} [يوسف: 47]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven severe years are years of drought and famine that consume the food stored during the seven fertile years.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن} [يوسف: 48] يقول يأكلن ما كنتم اتخذتم فيهن من القوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The years are rhetorically described as eating, although their inhabitants eat the stored food; the line about day as heedlessness and night as sleep illustrates this attribution.
rows.anchor: {يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون} [يوسف: 48]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥṣunūn means to secure or store a small remainder; iḥṣān literally means putting something in a protected place, hence preserving it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {إلا قليلا مما تحصنون} [يوسف: 48] يقول: تخزنون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada calls the severe years drought and says they consume the provisions gathered earlier, leaving only what people store.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: " {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك سبع شداد} [يوسف: 48] وهن الجدوب المحول، {يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون} [يوسف: 48]

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what you preserve as what you store or secure.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {إلا قليلا مما تحصنون} [يوسف: 48] يقول: تخزنون

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the preserved remainder as what people raise or save.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، " {يأكلن ما قدمتم لهن إلا قليلا مما تحصنون} [يوسف: 48] قال: مما ترفعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forecast of a final year of relief was not part of the king's dream; God taught Yusuf this unseen knowledge as a sign of his prophethood and truthfulness.
rows.anchor: ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God gave Yusuf knowledge of an additional year about which the people had not asked.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " ثم زاده الله علم سنة لم يسألوه عنها، فقال: {ثم يأتي من بعد ذلك عام فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون} [يوسف: 49]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yugāth al-nās means people receive rain and relief from rainfall.
rows.anchor: {فيه يغاث الناس} [يوسف: 49]

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the year in which people receive relief as a year of rain.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {فيه يغاث الناس} [يوسف: 49] بالمطر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities explain 'they press' as pressing grapes, sesame, oil, olives, and other fruits in the fertile year.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {وفيه يعصرون} [يوسف: 49] السمسم دهنا، والعنب خمرا، والزيتون زيتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second interpretation attributed to Ibn Abbas takes the verb as milking; a reading with tā' makes the audience the ones who milk.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، " {وفيه يعصرون} [يوسف: 49] قال: فيه يحلبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Regional readers transmit ya' for people pressing produce and ta' for directly addressing the audience; al-Tabari accepts either established reading because they agree in meaning.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك أن لقارئه الخيار في قراءته بأي القراءتين الأخريين شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported ya' reading meaning 'they are rained upon' is not acceptable because it conflicts with the established readings of the regional readers.
rows.anchor: وقرأه بعضهم: «وفيه يعصرون» بمعنى: يمطرون، وهذه قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها لخلافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari rejects interpreting ya'sirun as escaping drought through rain by analogy with al-'asr meaning rescue; poetry cannot outweigh the unanimous interpretation of the Companions and Successors.
rows.anchor: وذلك تأويل يكفي من الشهادة على خطئه، خلافه قول جميع أهل العلم من الصحابة والتابعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation transmitted through al-Faraj ibn Fadala from Ali ibn Abi Talha has no sound meaning because it conflicts with known Arabic and Ibn Abbas's usage.
rows.anchor: وأما القول الذي روى الفرج بن فضالة عن علي بن أبي طلحة، فقول لا معنى له، لأنه خلاف المعروف من كلام العرب
